submission.reasoning: An elevated interactive cmd.exe (proc-690e6c933a), run by WORKSTATION5\wardog on workstation5, ran three commands in order. First, sc.exe (proc-f4d3576242) repointed the Fax service binPath to 'powershell.exe -noexit -c write-host T1543.003 Test'. Second, 'sc start Fax' (proc-cd222a569d) started the service, which launched the PowerShell payload as NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE (proc-7f9f3418e9). Third, about 6 seconds later, sc.exe (proc-babd722e6c) set the binPath back to fxssvc.exe. This is MITRE technique T1543.003: hijacking a Windows service to run code with service privileges. The command line matches the Atomic Red Team test of that name, so this may be an authorised emulation, but the activity itself is real service hijacking and code execution. No Fax service registry record turned up in searches, so the restored binPath should be checked on the host.
